title: HPSF Outlines SC26 Tutorials, Workshops and Community Events - HPCwire

Off the Wire Press Releases

HPSF Outlines SC26 Tutorials, Workshops and Community Events

Nov. 15, 2026 — Join the High Performance Software Foundation (HPSF) team this week in Chicago at SC26 for a packed week of conversations at the HPSF booth and sessions on the SC26 agenda that feature HPSF projects including tutorials, workshops, papers, panels, BoFs, and posters.

Be sure to visit the HPSF booth (#6409) where you can chat with technical representatives of HPSF projects like Spack, Kokkos, Chapel, CharlieCloud, E4S, Environment Modules, ClusterShell, and more on the latest developments and tools in high performance software.

HPSF supports projects that advance portable software for diverse hardware by increasing adoption, aiding community growth, and enabling development efforts. HPSF is lowering barriers to productive use of today’s and future high performance computing systems and the team can’t wait to speak with you at SC26.

Sessions

Planning your schedule for SC26? Make sure to join the presentations featuring HPSF project maintainers and community leaders:

Sunday, November 15

  • A tutorial for Kokkos: Performance Portability for C++ Applications and Libraries (8:30am – 5:00pm CST)
  • Using Containers to Accelerate HPC (8:30am – 5:00pm CST)
  • Flux: Workload Management for HPC and AI/ML Simulation in Cloud (8:30am – 12:00pm CST)
  • 14 GPU Programming Paradigms Put to the Test: Performance Portability and Halstead Difficulty in Scientific Computing (9:40am – 10:00am CST)
  • Descriptive Execution of HPC Applications and Workflows (9:50am – 10:00am CST)
  • LLMs as Packagers of HPC Software (11:20am – 11:30am CST)
  • A Performance-Portable GPU-Accelerated Solution for Particle-Particle Particle-Mesh Method using Cabana and FFTX (11:42am – 12:06pm CST)
  • Reproducible Benchmarking for High-Performance Computing Applications (1:30pm – 5:00pm CST)
  • A Locality-Aware Execution Model for Distributed Graph Algorithms using NWGraph and HPX (3:50pm – 4:10pm CST)
  • The Price of a Single Source: Performance Portability of Chapel and Julia across CPUs and GPUs (3:54pm – 4:18pm CST)
  • Performance Improvement of Multi-Dimensional Parallel Loops in Kokkos (4:18pm – 4:42pm CST)
  • Scalable AMG Preconditioning for DG Neutron Diffusion Solvers on Manycore CPUs (4:30pm – 4:50pm CST)
  • Energy-Aware Performance Characterization of Kokkos Kernels Across Precision Levels (4:52pm – 5:04pm CST)

Monday, November 16

  • Managing HPC Software Complexity with Spack Tutorial (8:30am – 5:00pm CST)
  • E4S: An HPC-AI Software Ecosystem for Science Workshop (9:00-9:20am CST)
  • Building a Kubernetes-first, sovereign HPC system: OpenCUBE (9:40am – 10:00am CST)
  • Benchmarking Agentic AI Workflows with Charliecloud (9:50am – 10:00am CST)
  • OpenCHAMI for Deployment of Inference Services (10:30am – 11:00am CST)
  • Stress-Testing Exascale Scientific Data Output – ADIOS2 Configuration Strategies for WarpX under Extreme Load Imbalance (11:50am – 12:10pm CST)
  • Correctness Evidence for I/O Optimizations in VPIC-Kokkos: Preliminary Results (12:10pm – 12:15pm CST)
  • Workload-Manager-Agnostic QPU Integration with QRMI (1:30pm – 5:00pm CST) Flux Framework demo/presentation will start around 4pm CST
  • Software for Large Scale Application (2:00pm-3:00pm CST)
  • The case for unprivileged containerization in HPC, or: Does software simplicity still matter in 2026? (2:00pm – 2:40pm CST)
  • Platform-Agnostic Kernel Fusion Pipeline for Linear Algebra Kernels in MLIR (2:23pm – 2:30pm CST)
  • Charliecloud: Image Build Optimization for AI Workloads (2:40pm – 2:50pm CST)
  • CI for E4S: Build and Test Automation for a Containerized HPC-AI Software Stack Workshop (3:30pm – 4:00pm CST)
  • Security and Day-2 Resilience as First Class Control Plane Primitives for Heterogeneous Supercomputers (4:25pm – 4:50pm CST)
  • Overlay Containers in Apptainer (4:30 – 4:40 CST)

Tuesday, November 17

  • Posters (10:00am – 5:00pm CST):
    • Union of Containers: Layered Software Stacks with Cross-Container Dependency Reuse for HPC
    • Scalable OpenCHAMI Node Infrastructure Collection (SONIC)
    • A Viskores-Enhanced Vision Transformer Framework for MRI-Based Cancer Image Classification on Frontier
    • Correlation-Aware Uncertainty Visualization of Multivariate Data with Many-Core Acceleration
  • Interactive Debugger for Performance Portable Python HPC Kernels (11:37am – 12:00pm CST)
  • OpenCHAMI Community Birds of a Feather (12:15pm – 1:15pm CST)
  • The Impact of GenAI on HPC Programming and Programming Models Birds of a Feather (12:15pm – 1:15pm CST)
  • OpenACC Forum – The Future of Programming Accelerators with Directives (5:15pm – 6:45pm CST)

Wednesday, November 18

  • The Future of the HPC Workforce: Skills, Scale, and Sustainability Panel (12:15pm – 1:15pm CST)
  • Spack User Group Happy Hour, Sponsored by Susquehanna (6:30 – 9:30pm CST) More details below.

Thursday, November 19

  • Designing Open, Heterogeneous System Monitoring Around OpenCHAMI (12:15pm – 1:15pm CST)
  • Posters (1:45pm – 2:00pm CST):

Friday, November 20

  • Performance-Portable Exact Gaussian Process Regression in Python via SYCL and oneMath (9:46am – 10:00am CST)
  • Porting and Benchmarking Chapel on Emerging RISC-V Hardware: An HPC Viability Study Workshop (10:30am – 10:40am CST)

Come to the Spack User Group Happy Hour

On Wednesday evening, relax and connect at the Spack User Group Happy Hour, sponsored by Susquehanna from 6:30 – 9:30pm CST. Join the Spack team and Susquehanna for a casual evening of food, drinks, networking, and swag during SC26. Come meet fellow Spack users, developers, and contributors. Register here.

Meet HPSF community at SC

Dive into technical sessions, connect with the HPSF project community, and explore the future of open source high-performance computing at SC26. See you at SC26!
